lead: Cockroach Labs ships a Db2 migration built entirely by agents inside its coding hospital, byte-level Transformers challenge the tokenizer, and fake Claude installers ride Google ads through Bing redirects.

sections.title: The coding hospital
sections.intro: Cockroach Labs runs coding agents like a medical team, and a hobby OS wants agents at the kernel.

sections.title: Do models need tokenizers
sections.intro: Flat byte-level Transformers catch and pass subword models as they scale.

sections.title: Fake Claude installers
sections.intro: Malvertising abuses Bing redirects to push ClickFix attacks dressed as Claude.

sections.title: Decompiling games, at industrial scale
sections.intro: A three-month, 500-billion-token FPS recreation, and the Kotaku wave of browser ports driven by Opus 5.5.

sections.title: Agent tooling and toys
sections.intro: A stand-up call for your Claude Code session, a Rust engine for agent-made 3D video, and Python 3.15 in Actions.

sections.title: Research, models and money
sections.intro: Models fall short of a human algorithmic innovation, Microsoft ships a decision model, and two raises land.

sections.title: Humans, tools and the AI backlash
sections.intro: Today's reading is about what AI does to people and creative work: a premium on human-made art, a study on persistence, an actor refusing an AI waiver, and an AI-built Adobe clone.

sections.title: Robots, data and road tolls
sections.intro: Physical AI funding built on filmed human work, plus a data page on European driving costs.
